title: Morse index and nullity of rotationally symmetric $Y$-singular minimal surfaces: the resonant surface $Y_{\pi/6}$ (Theorem 4.11)
author: Elham Matinpour
work: Morse index and nullity of rotationally symmetric $Y$-singular minimal surfaces
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Theorem 4.11 (source0.tex lines 1728-1730, printed on page 30 of the published version), the culminating classification statement of the paper: the resonant surface Y_{pi/6} has Morse index two and nullity five. The retained complete proof (lines 1732-1930) is a genuine 199-line variational computation, not a routine verification: it treats each angular frequency separately, computes the one-dimensional catenoidal index forms together with their boundary terms, controls all positive-frequency forms by an explicit estimate, identifies the n=0 and n=1 weak kernels explicitly, cuts the two-dimensional radial weak kernel down to one dimension by testing against the missing direction psi, and assembles the nullity count from the zero-trace and boundary kernels. The residual difficulty is the case analysis exactly at the resonant parameter, where one catenoidal face has T=0 and the usual nondegeneracy of the radial sector fails, so the boundary-pairing identities and the zero-trace/boundary index decomposition have to be tracked by hand. That is research-level geometric analysis, well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying exercises, where such index computations are quoted rather than carried out.
